title: Pre-Analysis — Full Spectrum Ceiling and Wall Wash Lighting with Scene Control

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Lighting — Ceiling and Wall Wash Lights

abstract: Work order on the full spectrum cabin lighting installation, cancelled part way through when the emitter supplier changed and the cabin definition office took ownership of the configuration question.

sections.objective: Establish what the full spectrum ceiling and wall wash emitter with scene sequencing disturbs in the crown space above the ceiling panels, and whether the additional heat load and the new control run affect anything already installed at the same stations. The work order was raised by the cabin systems office ahead of the first customer definition meeting, with the intention of producing a clean installation envelope before any layout was offered.
sections.findings_summary: Only the crown space results were completed before the work order was stopped. The trim air riser and its regulating valve occupy the crown volume at the forward zone station where the new emitter channel is deepest, and the two have never been drawn on the same section; the emitter channel as proposed leaves no removal path for the valve. The valve removal task confirms this from the other side: it calls for the ceiling panel to be dropped along the full bay, which the continuous emitter channel would prevent. The fault isolation procedure for a cabin zone out of band was noted as a third item because it sends the mechanic into the same crown space, but the assessment was not finished. The supplier change arrived at that point and the remaining scope moved to the cabin definition office with the configuration question.
sections.next_steps: Close this work order and transfer the open items to the cabin definition dossier, which now owns the emitter selection and therefore the channel depth. Pass the crown space section drawing and the two air conditioning findings across so the removal path question is not rediscovered. Recommend that the definition office ask for a segmented emitter channel rather than a continuous one, since that resolves the removal path without a layout change. No position is taken here on the installation itself.

similarity_seeds: scene sequencing driven from the cabin attendant panel
full spectrum emitter replacing a three colour ceiling wash

tasks.title: Map the crown volume at the emitter channel stations
Check removal paths for equipment above the ceiling panels
Assess the additional heat load on the crown space

expected_findings.rationale: The trim air riser and its regulating valve sit in the crown volume at the forward zone station where the proposed emitter channel is deepest. The two installations have never been drawn on one section and, as proposed, the channel leaves the valve no removal path. Nothing in the two texts overlaps; only the cabin zone links them.
expected_findings.resolution: Ask the definition office for a segmented emitter channel, which resolves the removal path without a layout change.

expected_findings.rationale: The valve removal calls for the ceiling panel to be dropped along the full bay. A continuous emitter channel prevents that, which turns a line task into a cabin strip and would be discovered by the first operator to try it.
expected_findings.resolution: Transfer to the cabin definition dossier with the channel depth question.

expected_findings.rationale: The out-of-band isolation procedure sends the mechanic into the same crown space at the same station. The assessment of what the emitter channel does to that access was not completed before the work order was stopped.
expected_findings.resolution: Hand over as an open item; no conclusion reached here.

type_data.conclusion: Work order cancelled at the supplier change. The crown space findings and the open heat load item are transferred to the cabin definition dossier, which now owns the configuration.
